ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$, with $E$ being a point on the extension line of diameter $AB$, and $AB \parallel DC$. If $\angle A=70^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle CBE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $O$,\\
it follows that $\angle A+\angle C=180^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle A=70^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle C=110^\circ$,\\
Since $AB\parallel DC$,\\
it follows that $\angle CBE=\angle C=110^\circ$;\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{110^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: As can be seen from the attached figure, there is quadrilateral ABCD inside the circle, AB is a horizontal diameter, and point O is on AB; point E is on the extension line of AB to the right past B. Points D and C are located below the circle, and segment DC is also horizontal, parallel to AB and BE. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, its opposite angles are supplementary, that is, ∠A+∠C=180°. It is known that ∠A=70°, therefore ∠C=180°−70°=110°. Also because DC∥AB, and E is on the extension line of AB, DC∥BE; then by the corresponding angle relationship of parallel lines, ∠CBE is equal to ∠BCD, that is, ∠C. Therefore ∠CBE=110°.
